question: The bile produced by the liver is stored in the gallbladder from where it is secreted into the duodenum when the muscles involved receive this order in the form of hormonal and nervous signals mediated by:
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Cholecystokinin" -> "stimulates gallbladder contraction" -> "bile secretion into duodenum" -> "parasympathetic activation" -> "enhanced digestive process" -> 95%
CHAIN: "Secretin" -> "stimulates pancreatic bicarbonate secretion" -> "neutralizes stomach acid in duodenum" -> "parasympathetic activation" -> "enhanced digestive process" -> 70%
CHAIN: "Colecitocinin" -> "possible confusion with cholecystokinin" -> "beta-adrenergic sympathetic activation" -> "unclear effect on bile secretion" -> 50%
CHAIN: "Pancreozimine" -> "possible confusion with pancreozymin (cholecystokinin)" -> "beta-adrenergic sympathetic activation" -> "unclear effect on bile secretion" -> 50%
CHAIN: "Secretin" -> "stimulates pancreatic bicarbonate secretion" -> "neutralizes stomach acid in duodenum" -> "alpha-adrenergic sympathetic activation" -> "unclear effect on bile secretion" -> 60%
analysis: The release of bile from the gallbladder into the duodenum is primarily stimulated by the hormone cholecystokinin (CCK), which is released in response to the presence of fats in the duodenum. CCK causes the gallbladder to contract and the sphincter of Oddi to relax, allowing bile to flow into the duodenum. This process is also supported by parasympathetic nervous system activation, which further stimulates gallbladder contraction. Therefore, the correct combination of hormonal and nervous signals is cholecystokinin and parasympathetic activation.
